title: What is the order of rotation of each of six figures?
description: Six figures, each with a dot at its centre, are turned one by one, and the turns that fit are counted with the full turn included. The count is checked by multiplying the order by the smallest turn to get the full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: the order of rotational symmetry is the number of turns that fit, and the full turn is one of them. Watch for students who leave the full turn out of the count.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (section 9.2, first block)
video_script.why: The child counts how often a figure fits itself in one full turn, counting the full turn as one match.
video_script.substitution: turn each figure about its dot and count the turns that fit, the way the book counts for the windmill
video_script.anchor: the six figures of the book question, each with a dot at its centre
video_script.payoff_line: The orders are two, four, six, three, four and five

final_answer.spoken: the orders are two, four, six, three, four and five

maths_rules: order of rotational symmetry = number of angles of symmetry = number of turns that fit in one full turn, counting 360°
the book's windmill fits at 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°, so its order is 4
flagged slanted line: fits after 180° and 360°, order 2
two crossing lines at right angles: fits after 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°, order 4
six pointed star with equal points: 360 ÷ 6 = 60, order 6
plus shape with four equal arms: 360 ÷ 4 = 90, order 4
video_script.design: The six figures from the book question, each drawn with a dot at its centre. Each is turned and the fits are counted. A last check multiplies each order by its smallest turn to get the full turn.
open_questions: The crossing-lines figure is read as two lines crossing at a right angle (order 4, as the book answer says). If the marked angle at the top is not a right angle, its order would be 2.

<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then the three bent arms, the plus shape and the pentagon.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many turns fit each figure, counting the full turn?

beats.on_screen: Given: six figures, each with a dot at its centre
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six figures, and each has a dot at its centre.

beats.on_screen: To find: the order of rotational symmetry of each figure
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the order of rotational symmetry of each figure.

beats.on_screen: order = number of turns that fit in one full turn, 360° counted

marks.rule: the rule order = number of turns that fit is written
marks.full: the full turn 360° is underlined in the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, we work the same way as the example in your book.
Turn each figure about its dot, and count the turns that fit.
<bookmark mark='full'/>Count the full turn too.

beats.on_screen: flagged line: fits after 180° and 360°, so 2 turns; crossing lines at right angles: fit after 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°, so 4 turns

marks.line: the flagged line turns by 180° and a tick appears
marks.full: the flagged line turns by 360° and a second tick appears
marks.cross: the crossing lines turn by 90° each time, and four ticks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Step two, the flagged line fits after a half turn of one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='full'/>It fits again after the full turn, so its order is two.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>The crossing lines meet at right angles.
They fit after ninety, one hundred eighty, two hundred seventy and three hundred sixty degrees.
Its order is four.

beats.on_screen: star with 6 equal points: 360° ÷ 6 = 60° per turn, so 6 turns; three bent arms: 360° ÷ 3 = 120° per turn, so 3 turns

marks.arms: 360° ÷ 3 = 120° is written beside the three bent arms

narration: <bookmark mark='star'/>Step three, the star has six equal points, and three hundred sixty divided by six is sixty degrees.
Its order is six.
<bookmark mark='arms'/>The three bent arms are equal, and three hundred sixty divided by three is one hundred twenty degrees.
Its order is three.

beats.on_screen: plus shape with 4 equal arms: 360° ÷ 4 = 90° per turn, so 4 turns; regular pentagon with 5 equal sides: 360° ÷ 5 = 72° per turn, so 5 turns

marks.plus: 360° ÷ 4 = 90° is written beside the plus shape

narration: <bookmark mark='plus'/>Step four, the plus shape has four equal arms.
Three hundred sixty divided by four is ninety degrees, so its order is four.
<bookmark mark='pent'/>The pentagon has five equal sides.
Three hundred sixty divided by five is seventy two degrees, so its order is five.

marks.mul: the first three products are written one under the other
marks.rest: the last three products are written
marks.all: each product is ticked and shows 360°

narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Step five, check by multiplying the order by the smallest turn.
Two by one hundred eighty, four by ninety, and six by sixty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Three by one hundred twenty, four by ninety, and five by seventy two.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Each one gives three hundred sixty degrees, the full turn.

beats.on_screen: Answer: flagged line 2, crossing lines 4, star 6, three bent arms 3, plus shape 4, pentagon 5
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The orders are two, four, six, three, four and five.
